review_scope: Local speech runtime and release acceptance; no live settings or system packages changed

tested_runtime.system_info: WHISPER : COREML = 0 | OPENVINO = 0 | CPU : SSE3 = 1 | SSSE3 = 1 | AVX = 1 | AVX2 = 1 | F16C = 1 | FMA = 1 | OPENMP = 1 | REPACK = 1 |
tested_runtime.interpretation: The isolated test wheel decoded on CPU. A true use_gpu preference does not establish GPU support or GPU execution. This does not inspect the installed desktop runtime.

distribution_findings.desktop_whisper_install: packaging/build-desktop.sh installs the voice extra with --only-binary pywhispercpp
distribution_findings.upstream_windows_wheels: Upstream documents basic CPU PyPI wheels; its wheel workflow has no CUDA or Vulkan build option for Windows
distribution_findings.upstream_acceleration_route: CUDA or Vulkan support requires a corresponding native source build and toolchain
distribution_findings.piper_residency: Available when a compatible Piper Python API is installed; explicit custom binaries and missing APIs retain the CLI fallback
distribution_findings.piper_default_bundle: The voice extra currently declares pywhispercpp and cloud transcription dependencies, not piper-tts

acceptance_limits: Warm Piper first-audio evidence demonstrates worker reuse, not cold latency or desktop sandbox availability
Browser evidence demonstrates synthetic capture tail flushing and continuous scheduling, not recorded microphone quality
CPU Whisper timings were measured under concurrent workloads and are not controlled before-and-after benchmarks
The large model did not achieve real-time recognition in this environment
A smaller model showed transcription errors on the same Mandarin sample; changing model size cannot be described as an accuracy-neutral fix
No GPU build, device inference, or GPU release artifact was verified
bounded_gpu_distribution_followup: Build a Windows x64 Python 3.12 wheel from an exact pywhispercpp release and its pinned whisper.cpp submodule, using GGML_CUDA=1 and a toolkit compatible with the supported GPU architectures
Keep the experiment in an isolated build environment; record compiler, toolkit, target architectures, dependencies, wheel filename and digest
Install that wheel into a clean isolated runtime and prove actual device inference on a supported GPU, plus import and CPU fallback on a machine without that GPU
Repeat synthetic Mandarin recognition with fixed text, model digest and audio digest; record cold loading, first and repeated warm decoding, transcription errors, cancellation, and resident memory

Only after successful runtime verification, teach desktop packaging to consume that authenticated wheel and its redistributable native dependencies; never infer GPU execution from use_gpu or a successful package import
